glossary.definition: The role accountable for decisions and review of a defined process.
An agreed statement of where mapped work starts and ends, naming the triggering event, the output, and the recipient, without implying that work outside the boundary is unimportant.
The point at which one role transfers an output to the next role, complete only when the receiving role has the information needed to act.
A structure for grouping and relating an organization's processes so that readers can find work, understand relationships, and trace connections between overview and detail.

The entry point to a process architecture, showing agreed process groups and their relationships at a level of detail sufficient for a reader to find a process and identify adjacent processes without a presenter.
A represented relationship between two processes at the overview level, identifying what one process provides to another and who is accountable for an open issue on that connection.
A controlled test of a small representative sample of selected maps and decisions, performed before committing to a full migration, with agreed acceptance criteria and retained evidence.
The organizational decision to rely on the new arrangement for an agreed scope, made after reviewing pilot results, open discrepancies, and a tested recovery route.
A document identifying the source file, intended scope, expected relationships, permitted sample, known limitations, and the person who will accept or escalate the result.
A structured list of candidate process maps, each with its purpose, scope, source location, format, acceptance owner, and status, used to guide selection and decisions before a pilot.
